at elske.explanation: "At elske" means "to love". It is a strong word, kept mostly for people you truly care about: "Jeg elsker dig" (I love you). For things and activities, Danes usually say "Jeg kan godt lide" (I like) or "Jeg holder af" (I am fond of). Saying you "elsker" (love) pizza is possible, but it sounds playful.

sentence.da: Hun vil **elske** sine børn for evigt.
sentence.en: She will love her children forever.

e-boks.explanation: "En e-Boks" means "an e-Boks", the digital mailbox where public offices, banks and companies send you letters.

forms.da: Jeg har et brev i e-Boks.
forms.en: I have a letter in e-Boks.

sentence.da: Jeg har fået et brev i **e-Boks**.
sentence.en: I have received a letter in e-Boks.

efter.explanation: "Efter" means "after": "efter arbejde" (after work). In some phrases it means "for": "at lede efter nøglerne" (to look for the keys). Before a whole sentence, say "efter at": "efter at jeg kom hjem" (after I came home).

sentence.en: We go for a walk after dinner.

egen.explanation: "Egen" means "own", and it goes with words like "min" (my) or "din" (your): "mit eget værelse" (my own room), "mine egne ting" (my own things).

sentence.en: I have my own car.

ekstra.explanation: "Ekstra" means "extra", more than you already have. Before another word it makes that word stronger: "ekstra god" (extra good).

sentence.da: Vi skal have en **ekstra** stol, tak.
sentence.en: We need an extra chair, please.

eller.explanation: "Eller" means "or": "te eller kaffe?" (tea or coffee?). Added at the end of a question, it asks for agreement, like "right?": "Du kommer, eller?" (You are coming, right?). Don't mix it up with "ellers" (otherwise): "Skynd dig, ellers kommer vi for sent" (Hurry up, or we will be late).

sentence.en: Do you want tea or coffee?

ellers.explanation: "Ellers" means "otherwise" or "or else": "Skynd dig, ellers kommer vi for sent" (Hurry up, or else we will be late). It also means "else" in questions: "Hvad ellers?" (What else?). Don't mix it up with "eller" (or): "te eller kaffe" (tea or coffee).

forms.da: skynd dig, ellers kommer vi for sent
forms.en: hurry up, or else we will be late

sentence.da: Skynd dig, **ellers** kommer vi for sent.
sentence.en: Hurry up, or else we will be late.

elleve.explanation: "Elleve" means "eleven": "Jeg er elleve år gammel" (I am eleven years old).

sentence.en: I am eleven years old.

en e-mail.explanation: "En e-mail" means "an email". In daily speech people often shorten it to "en mail". You say "at sende en e-mail" (to send an email) and "at modtage en e-mail" (to receive an email).

sentence.en: I have sent you an email.

en eftermiddag.explanation: "En eftermiddag" means "an afternoon", the part of the day from lunch until evening. "Om eftermiddagen" means "in the afternoon", and "i eftermiddag" means "this afternoon". The word is built from "efter" (after) and "middag" (midday).

sentence.en: At four o'clock it is afternoon.

en elefant.explanation: "En elefant" means "an elephant". Notice the spelling with "f", not "ph".

sentence.en: An elephant is a big animal.

en elev.explanation: "En elev" means "a pupil", a child or young person who goes to school. It can also mean a trainee or apprentice at a workplace. Adults who study at university are usually called "en studerende" (a student) rather than "elev".

sentence.da: Min søn er **elev** i tredje klasse.
sentence.en: My son is a pupil in third grade.

en elevator.explanation: "En elevator" means "an elevator". Danes also say "en lift" (a lift). You go "med elevatoren" (by the elevator) up or down.

sentence.da: Vi tager en **elevator** op til femte sal.
sentence.en: We take an elevator up to the fifth floor.

en enkeltbillet.explanation: "En enkeltbillet" means "a one-way ticket". It is built from "enkelt" (single) and "billet" (ticket). The ticket for the trip back is "en returbillet" (a return ticket).

sentence.en: A one-way ticket to Copenhagen, please.

en euro.explanation: "En euro" means "a euro". Denmark uses "kroner" (crowns), not euros.

sentence.en: The ticket to Paris costs twenty euros.

end.explanation: "End" means "than": "Hun er højere end mig" (She is taller than me). It comes after words like "større" (bigger) or "bedre" (better). Don't use "som" for "than". "Som" means "as": "Han er lige så høj som mig" (He is as tall as me).

sentence.da: En bil er hurtigere **end** en cykel.
sentence.en: A car is faster than a bicycle.

endnu.explanation: "Endnu" means "yet" or "still". "Ikke endnu" means "not yet": "Har du spist? Nej, ikke endnu" (Have you eaten? No, not yet). With "en" it means "another": "endnu en kop kaffe" (another cup of coffee). Before a word like "bedre" it means "even": "endnu bedre" (even better).

sentence.en: I am not finished yet.

eneste.explanation: "Eneste" means "only" or "single", as in "the only one". It normally comes after "den", "det" or "de" (the): "den eneste" for en-words, "det eneste" for et-words. Do not mix it up with "kun" (just, only): "Jeg har kun én bil" (I have only one car).

sentence.en: He is the only doctor here.

engang.explanation: "Engang" (one word) means "once" or "some day", for a time you do not name exactly: "Der var engang..." (Once upon a time...), "Kom og besøg mig engang" (Come and visit me sometime). "En gang" (two words) means "one time": "en gang om dagen" (once a day).

forms.en: Come and visit me some day!

sentence.en: I once lived in Italy.

engelsk.explanation: "Engelsk" means "English", for the language and for things from England. As a school subject, say "Jeg har engelsk" (I have English, meaning an English lesson). Words for languages start with a small letter in Danish.

sentence.da: Hun er fra England og taler **engelsk**.
sentence.en: She is from England and speaks English.

england.explanation: "England" means "England". It is only one part of the United Kingdom; for Great Britain as a whole, say "Storbritannien" (Great Britain).

sentence.da: London er en stor by i **England**.
sentence.en: London is a big city in England.

enogtyve.explanation: "Enogtyve" means "twenty-one". Danish says the one first: "en-og-tyve" is literally "one-and-twenty". The same goes for 22, "toogtyve" (two-and-twenty), and 31, "enogtredive" (one-and-thirty).

sentence.en: My son is twenty-one years old.

enten…eller.explanation: "Enten … eller" means "either … or" and gives two choices: "Enten i dag eller i morgen" (Either today or tomorrow). "Enten" goes before the first choice and "eller" before the second. For "neither … nor", say "hverken … eller": "Jeg vil hverken have kaffe eller te" (I want neither coffee nor tea).

forms.da: Enten i dag eller i morgen.
Enten er du med, eller også er du ikke.
forms.en: Either you are in, or you are not.

sentence.en: We can either walk or take the bus.

er det ...?.explanation: "Er det ...?" means "is it ...?". Danish asks a question by putting "er" (is) first, with no extra word like "do": "Er det rigtigt?" (Is that right?). Fill the gap with whatever you want to ask about.

sentence.en: Is it far from here?

er du sikker?.explanation: "Er du sikker?" means "are you sure?". "Sikker" means "sure" or "safe". You can answer "Ja, helt sikker" (Yes, completely sure). To ask several people, say "Er I sikre?" (Are you all sure?).

sentence.da: **Er du sikker?** Det er en lang tur.
sentence.en: Are you sure? It is a long trip.

et efternavn.explanation: "Et efternavn" means "a last name", the family name you share with your family. It is made of "efter" (after) and "et navn" (a name).

sentence.en: My last name is Hansen.

et efterår.explanation: "Et efterår" means "an autumn" (or "a fall" in American English), the season between summer and winter. It is made of "efter" (after) and "et år" (a year).

sentence.da: Det er **efterår** med mange røde blade.
sentence.en: It is autumn with many red leaves.

et enkeltværelse.explanation: "Et enkeltværelse" means "a single room", a hotel room for one person. It is made of "enkelt" (single) and "et værelse" (a room).

sentence.da: Jeg rejser alene og vil have et **enkeltværelse**.
sentence.en: I travel alone and want a single room.

europa.explanation: "Europa" means "Europe". "Jeg bor i Europa" means "I live in Europe".

sentence.en: Denmark is in Europe.

europæisk.explanation: "Europæisk" means "European", for things that belong to Europe: "europæisk mad" means "European food" and "europæisk musik" means "European music".

sentence.en: Denmark is a European country.
